title: Positive-dimensional fibres of a proper image of a curve lift to contracted components
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $T,G,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume every irreducible component of $T$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $r:T\to G$ and $p:G\to Y$ be proper $k$-morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-scheme-over-base], with $r$ surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For any $y\in Y$ whose scheme-theoretic fibre $G_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has positive dimension, $y$ is a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] and there is an irreducible component $Z$ of $T$ such that $(p\circ r)(Z)=\{y\}$ and $\dim r(Z)=1$. Here $r(Z)$ is the image as a subset of $G$, with its subspace topology; it is closed because $r$ is proper. No separatedness over $k$, reducedness, or algebraic-closedness hypothesis on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, (2)(b)--(d) and its dimension/transcendence-degree computation; agent-extracted component/dimension consequence for proper images of pure one-dimensional finite-type schemes.

proof.text: Because $G_y$ is a finite-type scheme over the field $\kappa(y)$, it is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components. The hypothesis $\dim G_y>0$ therefore gives an irreducible component $W\subseteq G_y$ of positive dimension. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $W$ and choose a strict specialization $z$ of $\eta$ in $W$; thus $\eta\leadsto z$ is a chain of length one and $p(z)=y$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, preliminary fibre and component facts

proof.text: The positive-dimensional fibre makes $G$ nonempty, and surjectivity of $r$ then makes $T$ nonempty. The finite-type scheme $T$ is Noetherian, and its dimension is the maximum of the dimensions of its finitely many irreducible components; hence $\dim T=1$. Apply the image-dimension inequality in [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] to $r:T\to G$ to obtain $\dim\overline{r(T)}\leq1$. The image $r(T)$ is closed because $r$ is proper, and it equals $G$ because $r$ is surjective. Consequently $\dim G\leq1$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, dimension/image argument; properness gives closed image

proof.text: We claim that $y$ is closed. If it were not, choose a strict specialization $y_0$ of $y$ in $Y$. Let $C=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq G$ with its reduced closed-subscheme structure. The composite $C\hookrightarrow G\xrightarrow{p}Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c), so its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. This image contains $y$ and therefore contains $y_0$. Choose $z_0\in C$ with $p(z_0)=y_0$. Then $\eta\leadsto z\leadsto z_0$ is a strict chain of specializations in $G$, contradicting $\dim G\leq1$. Thus $y$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, component/dimension argument, with proper closed-image specialization

proof.text: Since $y$ is closed, $G_y$ is a closed subscheme of $G$, and its irreducible component $W$ is closed in $G$. Surjectivity of $r$ gives $x\in T$ with $r(x)=\eta$. Let $Z$ be an irreducible component of $T$ containing $x$, with its reduced induced closed-subscheme structure. The image $C=r(Z)$ is closed and irreducible, contains $W$, and satisfies $\dim C\leq\dim Z=1$ by the same image-dimension inequality. Since $W$ has positive dimension and is contained in $C$, it has dimension one; if $C$ strictly contains $W$, the generic point of $C$ followed by $\eta$ and then by a strict specialization in $W$ would give a chain of length two, again impossible. Hence $C=W$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, component/dimension count on the proper image of a curve

proof.text: Finally $p(r(Z))=p(W)=\{y\}$ because $W\subseteq G_y$. Therefore the irreducible component $Z$ of $T$ satisfies $(p\circ r)(Z)=\{y\}$ and $\dim r(Z)=\dim W=1$, as required.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, together with the proper closed-image and specialization argument; the statement is the extracted component/dimension consequence for a proper image of a pure one-dimensional finite-type scheme.
